mainTopic: The order of a fast day, and רב חסדא's rule on bathing in hot versus cold water on fasts and in mourning, with רבא's disagreement about an אבל
overview: The גמרא first finishes an earlier point. On a תענית ציבור the community deals with its problems first and prays afterward, as shown by two פסוקים in עזרא. Then רב חסדא teaches a new rule. When bathing is forbidden because of mourning (תשעה באב, an אבל), even cold water is forbidden. When it is forbidden only because bathing is a pleasure (a תענית ציבור), only hot water is forbidden. רב אידי בר אבין supports the fast-day leniency from the משנה's words 'they lock the bathhouses'. אביי objects, and רב שישא defends his father's proof. A proof for the strict half of the rule, from people who must immerse on תשעה באב, is pushed off with the hot springs of טבריא. Another ברייתא is used to attack the fast-day leniency, and the גמרא answers it. A story of a sage who bathed in cold water during שבעה is explained as a case of back-to-back mourning. Finally רבא rules that any אבל may bathe in cold water, and the גמרא begins a challenge to him that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not reverse the order of the fast day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the fast day could be flipped, with prayer first and community business afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of the fast day it just described. Earlier the town's problems came first and prayer came later, and now it asks why it can't be the other way around. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order taught before was: in the first part of the day, check the town's affairs; later, read from the תורה and pray. The question is that nothing so far forces that order. Maybe prayer should come first.

keyTerms.meaning: I can flip it around (a way of saying 'maybe it is the reverse')

phrases.english: I can reverse it!
phrases.notes: He means: maybe pray in the first part of the day, and deal with the town's problems afterward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order of the fast day taught just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order on a fast day: community matters first, then prayer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No source has been given for that order, so the reverse order should be just as possible.

steps.title: עזרא shows community matters come first, then prayer
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים in עזרא show he first dealt with the people's sin and only later, at the afternoon offering, rose to pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that! For it is written: 'Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered to me, because of the sin of the exiles.' And it is written: 'At the evening offering I rose from my fast and spread out my hands to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea of reversing the order. It brings proof from עזרא: first the people gathered around the community's problem, and only in the afternoon did he pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פסוק, people gather to עזרא because of the community's wrongdoing, which is the community business. In the next פסוק, at the time of the afternoon מנחה offering, he spreads his hands in prayer. The order in the פסוקים is the model: fixing community matters comes first, and prayer comes after.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't let that enter your mind; that idea is wrong
The wrongdoing of the people who came back from exile
The afternoon (evening) offering, meaning late in the day
And I spread out my hands (in prayer)

steps.whatToRemember: On a תענית ציבור, the community first looks into its own problems, and only afterward turns to prayer, just as עזרא did.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind, as it is written:
"Then everyone who trembled gathered to me
at the words of the God of Israel
because of the faithlessness of the exiles, etc.",
And it is written: "And at the evening offering
I arose from my fast
and spread out my hands to the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by bringing a source from the פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a פסוק that proves the original order.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe prayer could come first and community business later.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order in עזרא, first the community's sin and then prayer at מנחה, fixes the original order.

steps.title: Bathing: forbidden because of mourning versus forbidden because of pleasure
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that a ban on bathing that comes from mourning covers hot and cold water. A ban that comes from avoiding pleasure covers only hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: Whenever bathing is forbidden because of mourning, like תשעה באב or an אבל, it is forbidden in both hot and cold water. Whenever it is forbidden because of pleasure, like a תענית ציבור, hot water is forbidden and cold water is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רב חסדא gives a rule about which kind of bathing is forbidden on different sad days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It all depends on why bathing is forbidden. Mourning means removing all comfort, so even cold water is not allowed. On a תענית ציבור the goal is only to avoid enjoyment, and a cold wash is not really a pleasure, so it stays allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A public fast declared for the whole community (here, for lack of rain)

steps.confusionAlert: A תענית ציבור is still a real fast with a real ban on bathing. The difference is only in how far the ban reaches: hot water only, not cold.
steps.whyThisMatters: The reason behind a ban decides how far the ban goes. The rest of this section tries to find support for this rule in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said that Rav Ḥisda said:
Anything that is forbidden because of mourning,
for example, the Ninth of Av or a mourner,
is forbidden both in hot water and in cold water;
phrases.notes: He is talking about bathing. The word is left out here but assumed.

phrases.english: anything that is forbidden because of pleasure,
for example, a communal fast,
is forbidden in hot water, permitted in cold water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about bathing on fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ban from mourning covers hot and cold water. A ban from pleasure, like a תענית ציבור, covers hot water only.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: they lock the bathhouses
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין says the משנה supports רב חסדא, because it says only that the bathhouses are locked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: We also learned this in the משנה: 'And they lock the bathhouses.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי בר אבין brings support for רב חסדא from the משנה about the more serious fasts for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bathhouses were where people bathed in hot water. Since the משנה closes only the bathhouses, he reads it as forbidding only hot water, which matches רב חסדא's rule for a תענית ציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this (in a משנה), a way of bringing support

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
We, too, have learned this:
"And they lock the bathhouses."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב חסדא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that on a תענית ציבור only hot water is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'ונועלין את המרחצאות', closing only the hot bathhouses.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה could not have said to block the rivers
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. Even if cold water were forbidden, the משנה could not order the rivers blocked, so locking the bathhouses proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And if cold water were forbidden, should the משנה have taught 'they dam the rivers'?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רב אידי's proof. He says the משנה mentions only bathhouses because those are the only places that can actually be shut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can lock a building, but you cannot block a river. So the משנה's silence about cold water does not show that cold water is allowed. It may just be that there is no practical way to stop it.

keyTerms.meaning: Should it have taught? (a pushback asking what else it could have said)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And if bathing in cold water were forbidden,
"They dam the rivers,"
should the משנה have taught?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְאִי בְּצוֹנֵן אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רב חסדא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Locking the bathhouses was the only practical step possible, so it says nothing about whether cold water is allowed.

steps.title: רב שישא explains his father's proof: why mention bathhouses at all?
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא says his father's proof comes from the extra words. The משנה already forbade bathing, so 'lock the bathhouses' must be teaching that only hot bathing is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא, son of רב אידי, said: This is what bothered my father. We already learned that bathing is forbidden, so why do I need 'they lock the bathhouses'? Rather, learn from it: hot water is forbidden, cold water is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא defends his father's proof against אביי. He shows that the proof comes from the משנה repeating itself, not from what it could or could not block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said bathing is forbidden. Adding 'lock the bathhouses' would add nothing, unless it is telling us exactly what is forbidden: the hot bathhouses. So cold water is allowed, and רב חסדא's rule is supported after all.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what was hard for him; this is what bothered him
Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this

steps.whatToRemember: The proof does not come from what the משנה could practically block. It comes from the extra words: since bathing was already forbidden, 'lock the bathhouses' teaches that only hot water is forbidden on a תענית ציבור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defense backs up רב חסדא: on a תענית ציבור, washing in cold water is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
This is what was difficult for my father:
phrases.notes: His father is רב אידי בר אבין from step 4.

phrases.english: Since we learned: "forbidden in bathing,"
why do I need "they lock the bathhouses"?
Rather, is it not so? Learn from it:
in hot water it is forbidden, in cold water it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: אַבָּא הָכִי קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's rejection and brings back the proof from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the proof again, basing it on extra words in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof seemed to depend on the משנה choosing what to close, and אביי showed that rivers can't be closed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since bathing was already forbidden, 'lock the bathhouses' would be extra words, so it must teach that only hot water is forbidden.

steps.title: A proof from people who must immerse on תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows people who must immerse to do so on תשעה באב and יום הכפורים. Since immersion is only in cold water, this suggests that everyone else may not use even cold water, which supports רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports רב חסדא: 'All who must immerse may immerse as usual, on תשעה באב and on יום הכפורים.' In what water? If hot water, there is no immersion in hot water, because heated water is drawn water. So it must be cold water. Those who must immerse may do so, but anyone else may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב חסדא's rule that a mourning-based ban on bathing includes cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kosher immersion cannot be done in heated water, because heated water has been drawn into vessels. So the ברייתא must be talking about cold water. If only people who must immerse are allowed into cold water on תשעה באב, then everyone else is forbidden even in cold water, which is exactly רב חסדא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him: the opening of a proposed proof
People who are required to immerse in a מקוה to become pure
Drawn water, water that was in a vessel. It does not work for a kosher immersion

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:
All who are obligated in immersions
immerse in their usual way,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב בֵּין בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: both on the Ninth of Av and on Yom Kippur.
In what?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking what kind of water the ברייתא means: hot or cold.

phrases.english: If we say in hot water,
is there such a thing as immersion in hot water?
It is drawn water!
Rather, isn't it in cold water?
And those obligated in immersions, yes, they may;
another person, no, he may not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה in steps 4-6, the גמרא tries a second proof for רב חסדא from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that a mourning-based bathing ban (like תשעה באב) includes cold water
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא allowing those obligated in immersion to immerse on תשעה באב, which must mean cold water and implies others are forbidden

steps.title: The case is the hot springs of טבריא
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר קטינא says the ברייתא may be speaking about the natural hot springs of טבריא, where a kosher immersion in hot water is possible. So it says nothing about cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר קטינא said: The ברייתא was needed only for the hot springs of טבריא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנא בר קטינא pushes away the proof by showing the ברייתא could be talking about hot water after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the claim that immersion is impossible in hot water. But the springs of טבריא are naturally hot and were never drawn, so immersion there is kosher. The ברייתא may be permitting only that hot immersion, and cold water may be allowed for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for: the ruling applies to a narrow case
The natural hot springs of טבריא

phrases.english: Rav Ḥana bar Ketina said:
It was needed only for the hot springs of Tiberias.
phrases.notes: These springs come out of the ground hot, so the water was never drawn and a kosher immersion works there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 7 by reading the ברייתא as talking about naturally hot water.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The claim that immersion can never be in hot water is wrong. Natural hot springs are valid, so the ברייתא may be speaking about them and not about cold water.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא suggests cold water is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא says רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים gave up his immersion once a year for the sake of the בית המקדש. If cold water were allowed, he could simply have immersed in cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים said, 'The House of our God is worth losing an immersion for, once a year.' But if cold water is allowed, let him wash in cold water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חנא בר קטינא's answer from the last part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא skipped his immersion on תשעה באב in mourning for the בית המקדש. If cold water were permitted to everyone, there would be no loss at all, since he could immerse in cold water. His words suggest that cold water is forbidden too, which brings back רב חסדא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the end: look at the last part of the same source

phrases.english: If so, say the end of it:
Rabbi Ḥanina, the deputy High Priest, said:
The House of our God is worth it

phrases.aramaic: לְאַבֵּד עָלָיו טְבִילָה פַּעַם אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה.
phrases.english: to lose an immersion for its sake once a year.
phrases.notes: He means skipping his immersion on תשעה באב in mourning for the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: And if you say cold water is permitted,
let him wash in cold water!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in step 8 using the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנא בר קטינא's claim that the ברייתא is only about hot springs and that cold water may be allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If cold water were allowed, רבי חנינא would lose nothing, because he could immerse in cold water. His statement that he 'loses' the immersion implies cold water is forbidden.

steps.title: A place where there is no cold water
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that רבי חנינא was speaking about a place where only hot springs are available and there is no cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is talking about a place where cold water is not found.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends רב חנא בר קטינא's reading against the challenge from the end of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cold water may really be permitted. רבי חנינא lost his immersion only because where he was there were hot springs and no cold water. He gave up the hot immersion out of mourning, so the proof for רב חסדא falls away again.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not commonly found, is not available

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
In a place where cold water is not available.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the place had only hot springs
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא's loss of immersion shows cold water was forbidden to him.
steps.terutzMaskana: He had no cold water available, so his loss proves nothing about cold water. The proof for רב חסדא from this ברייתא is pushed off.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof for רב חסדא from this ברייתא was turned aside. The ברייתא can be read as speaking about the hot springs of טבריא, and רבי חנינא lost his immersion only because he was in a place with no cold water.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about fast days, mourners, and the person under a ban
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing the limits of the fast-day bans: work is forbidden only by day, shoes only in town, and bathing only of the whole body. It adds that the same is true for a מנודה and an אבל. The גמרא is setting up a proof that it will spell out next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: When they said work is forbidden, they meant only by day, but at night it is allowed. When they said wearing shoes is forbidden, they meant only in the city, but on the road it is allowed. How so? Going out on the road, he puts them on; coming into the city, he takes them off. When they said bathing is forbidden, they meant only the whole body, but face, hands, and feet are allowed. And you find the same for a person under a ban and for a mourner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempt to settle the question by quoting a ברייתא about fast days. This step only quotes the source, and the גמרא will draw the inference in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets the edges of each fast-day ban and then compares them to the rules of a מנודה and an אבל. Since an אבל is the clearest case of a mourning-based ban, this comparison is likely where the proof about cold water will come from.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a source brought as evidence
How so? Asking how the rule works in practice
A person placed under a ban (נידוי) by the court

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the proof inside this step yet. The ברייתא is only being quoted here, and the גמרא explains how it proves something in the next step.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
When they said 'forbidden to do work,'
they said it only for the daytime,
but at night it is permitted.
And when they said 'forbidden to wear shoes,'
they said it only in the city,
but on the road it is permitted.
How so?
When he goes out on the road, he puts on shoes;
when he enters the city, he takes them off.
And when they said 'forbidden to bathe,'
they said it only about his whole body,
but his face, hands, and feet are permitted,
and you find the same with a person under a ban and with a mourner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the immersion ברייתא was pushed off, the גמרא opens a fresh proof from a different ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רב חסדא is right that cold-water bathing is allowed on a תענית צבור. In step 12 this ברייתא is used to challenge that leniency.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the limits of fast-day bans and comparing them to a מנודה and an אבל. The inference comes in the next step.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to forbid even cold-water bathing on a public fast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the ברייתא must be about cold water. If so, washing the whole body is forbidden on a public fast even in cold water, which goes against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא's rule about all of them, including the מנודה and the אבל? Now, what kind of water is it talking about? If hot water, would an אבל really be allowed to wash his face, hands and feet? רב ששת said an אבל may not even put his finger into hot water! So it must be talking about cold water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the proof it set up in step 11. It shows that the ברייתא must be talking about cold water, and that creates a problem for רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says only whole-body washing is banned, and it says the same is true for an אבל. That means an אבל may wash his face, hands and feet. That cannot be about hot water, because רב ששת forbids an אבל to put even a finger in hot water. So the ברייתא must mean cold water, which would mean whole-body bathing in cold water is forbidden on a תענית צבור, against רב חסדא's leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: on all of them; the rule applies to every case listed
an אמורא whose ruling is used here to rule out hot water

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier, the support for רב חסדא from the ברייתא about immersion (steps 7-10) was actually pushed off, so his strictness for an אבל was never proven. The משנה proof in steps 4-6 backed his leniency for a תענית צבור, and now that same leniency is being attacked.

phrases.english: What, is it not referring to all of them,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the fast day, the מנודה and the אבל, which the ברייתא grouped together.

phrases.english: And with what are we dealing?
If we say with hot water:
are his face, his hands, and his feet permitted?
But didn't Rav Sheshet say:
A mourner is forbidden to stick his finger into hot water!
Rather, is it not about cold water!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the argument from the ברייתא quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that cold-water bathing is allowed on a תענית צבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא must be about cold water, since hot water is fully forbidden to an אבל. So whole-body bathing in cold water would be forbidden on a public fast.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about hot water; the comparison refers only to the other bans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about hot water. The line about the מנודה and the אבל refers to the other bans, not to bathing.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it really is about hot water. As for what bothered you, the line "and the same is true for a מנודה and an אבל": it refers to the rest of the rules, not to bathing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and saves רב חסדא. It says the ברייתא is about hot water after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole proof depended on the comparison to the אבל covering bathing too. If that line only covers work by day and shoes in town, nothing forces us to say the ברייתא means cold water. Then the ban on whole-body bathing on a fast is only about hot water, which fits רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually; keeping the original reading
a person placed under a ban
it refers to the rest (of the rules)

phrases.english: No, it really is about hot water.
And what was difficult for you,
"And the same you find with a person under a ban and a mourner":
it refers to the rest.
phrases.notes: "The rest" means the other limits in the ברייתא, like work only by day and shoes only in town.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a phrase in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to the מנודה and the אבל covers bathing too, which would force a cold-water reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison covers only the other bans, so the ברייתא can be about hot water, and רב חסדא stands.

steps.title: A mourner who bathed in cold water all seven days
steps.stepSummary: A story is brought in which רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא bathed in cold water throughout the seven days of mourning for his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אבא הכהן said in the name of רבי יוסי הכהן that the sons of רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא died, and he bathed in cold water all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that seems to go against the other half of רב חסדא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said an אבל may not bathe even in cold water. Here a great sage, while he was an אבל, bathed in cold water for the entire שבעה. That suggests cold water is allowed for an אבל.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear; introduces a new source
an incident, a story that happened

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא הַכֹּהֵן
phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Abba the priest said
in the name of Rabbi Yosei the priest:
There was an incident, and the sons died

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן רַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina,
and he bathed in cold water all seven days!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב חסדא's fast-day leniency, the גמרא tests his strictness for an אבל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that an אבל may not bathe even in cold water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sage in mourning bathed in cold water all seven days, which suggests cold water is permitted for an אבל.

steps.title: His mourning periods came one after another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי's mourning periods came back to back. In that special case a ברייתא allows some leniencies.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, his mourning periods came one right after another. As a ברייתא teaches: if someone's mourning periods came one after another and his hair grew heavy, he may lighten it with a razor and wash his clothes in water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the story is no proof. It was an unusual case, and it backs this up with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His sons died one after another, so his periods of mourning piled up. The ברייתא shows that in such a case the usual mourning bans are eased, such as cutting hair and washing clothes. The cold-water bathing belongs to that special leniency, so the normal rule for an אבל, as רב חסדא said, still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: his mourning periods came one right after another

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that back-to-back mourning periods have their own easier rules, without changing the basic bans of an אבל.

phrases.english: There it was when his mourning periods came one after another,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
If his mourning periods came one after another,
and his hair grew heavy, he may lighten it with a razor,
and he may wash his garment in water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the story in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a special situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story shows any אבל may bathe in cold water.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a case of back-to-back mourning, which has its own leniencies, so the general ban on an אבל stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's rule survives both tests: on a public fast cold water is allowed, and for an ordinary אבל even cold water is forbidden. The cold-water story was a special case of back-to-back mourning.

steps.title: רב חסדא sets the limits of the back-to-back mourning leniency
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the hair may be cut with a razor but not scissors, and clothes washed in plain water but not with natron or sand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: with a razor, but not with scissors. In water, but not with natron and not with sand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds details to the ברייתא from the last step and shows how far the leniency goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in the special case of back-to-back mourning, the leniency is limited. Each allowance in the ברייתא is held to the exact way it was stated: a razor and not scissors, plain water and not cleaning agents like natron or sand.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
With a razor, but not with scissors,
in water, but not with natron and not with sand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּתַעַר — אֲבָל לֹא בְּמִסְפָּרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the limits of the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In back-to-back mourning, hair may be lightened only with a razor, not scissors, and clothes washed only in plain water, not with natron or sand.

steps.title: רבא allows a mourner to bathe in cold water
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that an אבל may bathe in cold water during all seven days of mourning. He compares this to meat and wine, which an אבל is also allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A mourner may bathe in cold water all seven days. It is just like meat and wine, which he is also allowed to have.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a ruling: an אבל may wash in cold water for the whole שבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא disagrees with רב חסדא (step 3), who forbade an אבל to bathe even in cold water. The story of רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא was explained as a special case of back-to-back mourning, but רבא allows cold water for any אבל. His reason is that something pleasant is not forbidden just because it is pleasant: meat and wine are enjoyable, and an אבל may still have them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like… (a comparison to a known case)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the special case in step 15. That leniency was only for mourning periods that came back to back. רבא is now saying cold water is allowed for every אבל.

phrases.english: Rava said: A mourner is permitted to bathe
in cold water all seven days,
just as it is with meat and wine.
phrases.notes: A mourner may eat meat and drink wine even though he enjoys them. So enjoying a cold bath is fine too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָבֵל מוּתָּר לִרְחוֹץ בְּצוֹנֵן כׇּל שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagreeing with רב חסדא's ruling in step 3, רבא allows cold water for every אבל, not only in the special back-to-back case of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may bathe in cold water throughout שבעה, just as he may have meat and wine.

steps.title: A challenge to רבא is introduced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that it will bring a source to challenge רבא's ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to quote a source that seems to contradict רבא, and the source itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיתיבי always introduces a teaching from the time of the תנאים that seems to argue against what was just said. The target here is רבא's ruling that an אבל may bathe in cold water all seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאים-era source)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רבא's ruling in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that an אבל may bathe in cold water all seven days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source will be quoted that seems to forbid this bathing. The actual source appears in the next part of the text.
